snip.t: Infectious: HIV, TB (especially TB meningitis with nerve root involvement), malaria (cerebral malaria sequelae), hepatitis B/C, Campylobacter jejuni (classic GBS trigger), dengue, chikungunya
Shigella species, Campylobacter jejuni, and Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC) or Entamoeba histolytica.
Campylobacter jejuni — curved/comma or "seagull-wing" shaped gram-negative rod, classically associated with bloody diarrhea and a camping/outdoor exposure history

snip.t: Guillain-Barré syndrome — a post-infectious autoimmune complication; molecular mimicry between Campylobacter jejuni surface lipooligosaccharides and human peripheral nerve gangliosides triggers an autoimmune attack on nerve tissue

snip.t: About 75% of cases have a history of a preceding infection, including viral (cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus) and bacterial (Campylobacter jejuni) agents.
In the case of Campylobacter jejuni infection, this involves molecular mimicry.
